verdict.rationale: Logseq is open-source and local-first, storing all data as plain Markdown files on the user's own machine with no mandatory cloud backend, and users report self-managing sync/backup via their own GitHub repos — a de-facto form of self-hosting the core data layer. However, there is no official server/Docker deployment for running Logseq as a hosted service, and community evidence explicitly notes an unmet desire to 'self-host it as a website' with an outstanding, long-open GitHub feature request for that capability. Missing for 10: an official self-hostable server/web deployment option, first-party documentation of that deployment, and confirmation it works in practice (vs. an unresolved 1.8k-issue backlog).
